# Log in to Docker image repository

`docker login` is used to connect the local Docker client to the image repository. After successful login, `docker pull` and `docker push` will use the saved credentials to access private images or restricted resources.

## Log in to Docker Hub

Direct execution:

```bash
docker login
```

The new version of the Docker client can automatically use device codes for login on Docker Hub. The terminal will display a verification address and a one-time code, and authorization can be completed in a browser. If you need to explicitly specify an account, you can use:

```bash
docker login --username <docker-id>
```

## Log in to the self-built repository

In the command, only enter the repository host name and optional port; do not add the image path:

```bash
docker login registry.example.com
docker login registry.example.com:5000
```

## Using tokens in scripts

Automated scripts should not write passwords directly into the command line. Using `--password-stdin` can prevent passwords from appearing in the shell history and process list:

```bash
printf '%s' "$REGISTRY_TOKEN" | \
  docker login registry.example.com \
  --username "$REGISTRY_USER" \
  --password-stdin
```

`REGISTRY_TOKEN` should be injected by an interactive terminal, key management service, or continuous integration platform, and should not be written into tutorials, source code repositories, or image layers.

## Credential Storage and Exit

Docker typically writes the login configuration to `~/.docker/config.json`. If the system is configured with a credential store, the actual credentials are managed by the operating system keychain. Exit after using a public device or a short-term server:

```bash
docker logout
docker logout registry.example.com
```

## Verification and Debugging

```bash
docker info
docker pull hello-world:latest
```

- When `unauthorized` appears, first check the repository address, username, and token permissions.
- If you are logged in but still cannot push, verify that the image name contains the correct repository prefix and namespace.
- On servers without a graphical interface, if the keychain cannot be used, you can configure a available credential helper for the host, or use a short-term token with limited permissions.

Official reference: [Docker CLI `login`](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/login/).
